objective: Make model/runtime selection capability-aware, health-aware, cost-aware, privacy-aware, circuit-breaker protected, generation-fenced, and receipt-verifiable without treating model output as authority.

sources.finding: seL4 provides open-source microkernel isolation, controlled communication, and machine-checked functional-correctness proofs.
sources.impact: M230 uses controlled communication and explicit evidence boundaries but makes no formal-verification claim for FAISAL.

sources.finding: Unikraft documents minimal Linux-API-compatible library operating systems, hardware-level VM isolation, and fast cold starts for cloud-native workloads and AI agents.
sources.impact: FAISAL records runtime/backend capabilities as metadata and leaves minimal-VM qualification to a separate backend gate.

sources.finding: Cloud Hypervisor documents KVM/MSHV support, low-latency minimal VMM design, hotplug, migration, vhost-user offload, and experimental compatibility boundaries.
sources.impact: Route and execution receipts must bind backend identity/generation and fail closed when migration or snapshot compatibility is unknown.

sources.finding: LiteLLM documents multi-deployment routing, latency/cost/rate-limit strategies, cooldowns, fallbacks, weighted failover, concurrency limits, retries, and deployment-specific health tracking.
sources.impact: M230 implements a smaller deterministic provider-neutral contract with explicit circuit state and route receipts rather than embedding a gateway.

sources.finding: vLLM documents continuous batching, prefix caching, structured output, tools, tracing, speculative decoding, disaggregated serving, and broad model/hardware support.
sources.impact: M230 represents these as capability claims and does not claim vLLM execution or hardware performance.

sources.finding: SGLang documents radix/prefix caching, agentic and multimodal workflows, parallelism, and OpenAI-compatible serving.
sources.impact: Provider/runtime capability masks can express structured output, tools, multimodality, and related requirements without provider lock-in.

sources.finding: TensorRT-LLM documents hardware-specific KV-cache, batching, guided decoding, speculative decoding, quantization, and telemetry features.
sources.impact: Hardware-specific capabilities are admitted only as metadata until physical accelerator qualification exists.

sources.finding: OpenAI documents tool and function surfaces including web, file, MCP, and tool search.
sources.impact: A route selects a backend only; it never authorizes the model-requested tool.

sources.finding: OpenAI background mode documents asynchronous execution, polling, cancellation, and resumable cursors.
sources.impact: Background capability metadata is provider-neutral and requires separate execution authorization.

sources.finding: Anthropic documents structured client and server tool-use blocks and application-executed tool flows.
sources.impact: Tool-calling capability claims do not become authority.

sources.finding: Gemini documents parallel/compositional function calling and stateless replay of model steps and function results.
sources.impact: Request sequence, model generation, and route receipt fencing support replay-safe provider adapters.

features: provider-neutral capability masks for structured output tools background streaming vision speech embeddings multimodality citations and JSON schema
privacy locality hardware context and latency/cost admission
closed open and half-open circuit states
cloud fallback and recovery probe state
deterministic score and model-id tie break
request sequence and model generation fencing
SHA-256 route receipt binding request constraints selected backend and generation

validation.qemu_kernel_boot: FAISAL_M76_QEMU_VALIDATION_OK on ACPI-on one-vCPU 4G; FAISAL_INDUSTRY_SOAK_OK rounds=2 iterations_per_round=256

qualification_limits: This is a provider-neutral userspace routing contract, not a model-serving engine.
It does not claim model quality, hosted-provider availability, GPU performance, or equivalent functionality across providers.
No paid provider call, physical GPU/NPU, KVM microVM, independent builder, or independent security review was performed by this milestone.
Production release remains blocked by the project’s external evidence gate.
